ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the circuit diagram, the left side is the input voltage UI, and after passing through the CW7806 three-terminal voltage regulator, the output voltage UO is obtained on the right side; UO is the voltage of the upper output node on the right side relative to the bottom ground line. R1 is connected between the output node and the regulator common terminal node, and R2 is connected between this common terminal node and ground; the quiescent current IQ flowing into the common terminal node branch is also marked in the figure. Reasoning: Let the voltage of the common terminal node to ground be Vx. CW7806 is a 6 V voltage regulator, so it keeps UO - Vx = 6 V between the output terminal and the common terminal. The voltage across R1 is 6 V, so the R1 current is 6/R1. Writing KCL for the common terminal node, the current flowing through R2 to ground is Vx/R2, which is equal to the sum of the R1 current and IQ, namely Vx/R2 = 6/R1 + IQ. Therefore Vx = R2(6/R1 + IQ), UO = 6 + Vx. Substituting IQ = 1 mA = 0.001 A, R1 = 100 Ω, R2 = 200 Ω: UO = 6 + 200(6/100 + 0.001) = 6 + 200(0.061) = 6 + 12.2 = 18.2 V.

method.method_draft: Apply the lifted-ground fixed-regulator formula read from the image topology. First ignore IQ: the 6 V across R1 causes the divider to scale the output to 6(1 + R2/R1) = 6(1 + 200/100) = 18 V. Then include the regulator quiescent current shown entering the common node; it must flow through R2 to ground, adding IQ R2 = 0.001 * 200 = 0.2 V to the lifted common node and hence to UO. Therefore UO = 18 + 0.2 = 18.2 V.
